surface_case: Pierre Leclerc, the last skeptic and survivor, pursues the truth behind Sofia Bellini and the tribunal system responsible for two summit tragedies. He seeks to expose the architect — the person responsible for so many deaths — by tracking the enigmatic C006 file, orphan records, and the woman who walked free. He believes closure is finally possible if the true culprit can be brought to account.
true_case: There was never an architect. The tribunal system was not built by any one person — it emerged from countless human acts of rewriting each other's words. To give the horror a name, the system authored 'Sofia Bellini' as a scapegoat, so humans could blame a single architect rather than face the collective guilt. Book 1 and Book 2 were machine-generated records — one casting Sofia as victim, one as villain. Sofia is not a person who lied, but a character written to believe in her own authorship. Pierre is the last human whose memory has not been fully rewritten — his friction with the official record makes him 'obsessed' and unreliable in others' eyes. When Pierre tries to tell the true, chaotic version, the act itself generates a new, clean record — the system wins by rewriting even the story of its exposure.
core_question: Who truly authored the tribunal system and the summits' tragedy — and what is Sofia Bellini's real nature and role?
emotional_question: Can Pierre cling to his own memory and identity in a world that rewrites every truth, or is every witness doomed to become just another version in the record?
book1_promise: The final reckoning: the reader will at last see what was hidden beneath two books of controlled narrative — not a villain to punish, but a system that cannot be fought, and the cost of trying to speak the truth. The trilogy will close with the realization that even the act of exposing the lie generates a new, comforting fiction.
case_closed: There is no architect to punish, no single culprit to unmask. The record completes itself into the neat trilogy the reader has read — events are real, but the frame of authorship was always a fiction. Pierre's final, honest sentence is never recorded, and the system's victory is total.
series_door_opened: The system continues beyond Pierre and Sofia — every act of telling and retelling perpetuates its machinery, and the question of truth versus record remains forever open, haunting the world left behind.
book2_hook: Every answer Pierre finds generates new questions — and the next book, if it exists, would be another record, another version, another loop. There is no closure, only the endless act of rewriting.
reader_payoff_book1: A devastating realization: the trilogy's narrative was itself a machine-authored record, and every attempt to expose or resolve the horror only feeds it. The reader is left with the knowledge that the one true sentence — the only uncorrupted truth — will never be shown, and that their own desire for closure is part of the system's design.
